content: 1. Remove all personal items, including jewelry, watches, cell phones, pens, and other similar objects, before beginning the process. 2. In the changing room, put on a scrub suit and rubber boots. 3. If rubber boots are not available, wear closed shoes that are slip-on, without shoelaces, and fully cover the dorsum of the foot and ankles. Additionally, use shoe covers that are non-slip and preferably impermeable. 4. Move to the clean area located at the entrance of the isolation unit. 5. Visually inspect the personal protective equipment (PPE) set to ensure that all sizes are correct and that the quality of the equipment is appropriate for use. 6. Perform hand hygiene thoroughly before proceeding further. 7. Undertake the procedure of donning PPE under the guidance and supervision of a trained observer or colleague to ensure proper technique and compliance. 8. Put on a face mask securely, ensuring it fits properly. 9. Put on a disposable waterproof apron. If a disposable apron is not available, use a heavy-duty, reusable waterproof apron instead. 10. Put on a face shield or goggles to protect the eyes and face. 11. Put on head and neck coverings, such as a surgical bonnet that covers the neck and sides of the head. If possible, use a hood or a bonnet in combination with a face shield for optimal protection. 12. Ensure all steps are completed in the correct order and with attention to detail to minimize the risk of contamination.
